3 Tech Stock Ideas for Investors Planning for Retirement 
The tech sector is a very dynamic place. And for that reason, there are only so many large-cap tech companies that are worthy investment ideas for retirement-focused investors craving stability, low business risk and healthy dividend payments from their portfolio companies. 
If such investors also seek limited valuation risk, the number drops further still. Particularly in the current market environment. 
With that in mind, here are some large-cap tech stocks that could work for investors who are looking to buy and hold for a long time without having too much about the stability of the business that they’re betting on, and want to collect dividends along the way. 
Apple 
Apple (AAPL) is valued at 13 times at fiscal 2019 GAAP EPS consensus of $12.99. And that estimate might go up soon, should the company choose to deploy a large portion of the $207 billion in offshore cash it’s repatriating on stock buybacks. The dividend yield is at 1.5%, and might also soon go higher thanks to an overhauled capital return plan. 
With the smartphone, tablet and PC markets all fairly mature, Apple isn’t a company that’s likely to see tremendous long-term growth. But the company has been seeing healthy services and wearables growth, as it finds way to cross-sell products to and better monetize its huge iOS and macOS bases. Together with the potential for moderate share gains and average selling price (ASP) growth in its core business, and the possibility that a new needle-moving product (an AR headset?) could be launched at some point, this gives Apple a path towards seeing at least mid-to-high single digit sales in the years to come. 
Meanwhile, the stickiness of Apple’s software platforms and the power of its brand have produced exceptionally high loyalty rates within its hardware base. That loyalty keeps the risk of any massive sales decline pretty low. 
Microsoft 
Microsoft (MSFT) trades for 23 times a fiscal 2019 EPS consensus of $3.92. But the company’s near-term earnings are depressed by a shift in its revenue mix from up-front license sales to cloud subscriptions. Cash-flow multiples are lower: Microsoft’s enterprise value (market cap minus net cash) is equal to 17 times its fiscal 2019 free cash flow (FCF) consensus. The dividend yield is at 1.9%; as is the case for Apple, tax reform could motivate Microsoft to hike its dividend. 
The software giant has done a pretty good job of keeping its Windows cash cow stable in the face of ongoing PC sales pressures. And its other big cash cow, Office, is now seeing respectable growth as the Office 365 platform serves to grow the productivity suite’s addressable market. 
Microsoft also has several other growth drivers, from LinkedIn to its Azure public cloud platform (#2 behind Amazon Web Services) to its Dynamics business app suite (popular with small and mid-sized businesses). Along with buybacks and the operating leverage within Microsoft business model, these opportunities could help deliver low-double digit EPS growth in the years to come.

Texas Instruments 
Texas Instruments (TXN) trades for 18 times its 2019 GAAP EPS consensus of $5.67, and has an enterprise value equal to 16 times its expected 2019 FCF. The dividend yield is at 2.5%, and TI has committed to effectively returning all of its future FCF via dividends and buybacks. 
The chip giant is a leading player in plenty of lucrative analog, mixed-signal, microcontroller and DSP markets, and a well-diversified customer base that includes many blue-chip industrial, automotive, PC, smartphone and telecom equipment industry clients. About a fifth of its sales come from an automotive market that has been seeing solid growth as cars become more intelligent and electrified. And a little over a third comes from an industrial market seeing steady, moderate growth with the help of industrial automation and IoT hardware adoption. 
Throw in the modest share gains TI has been seeing in its core businesses, as well as ongoing buybacks and solid financial execution, and the company has a pretty good shot at keeping EPS growing at a double-digit clip in the coming years.
